Where it began

Kamindu Mendis was born in Galle on 30 September 1998 and went to Richmond College in his home town. At 13 he started bowling with both arms, and the habit stuck: he grew up able to bowl left-arm spin and right-arm off-spin in the same over.

He came up through Sri Lanka's youth teams, was picked for the Under-19 World Cup in 2016 and captained the side at the 2018 edition. His one-day debut for Sri Lanka followed in 2019, after a first T20 international against England in October 2018.

The player

His Test debut came against Australia in July 2022. He made a fifty and added 133 with Dinesh Chandimal, and Sri Lanka won by an innings, their first such win over Australia in Test cricket.

Then came a remarkable run. Against Bangladesh in March 2024, batting at number seven, he made 102 and 164 in the same match, the first batter ever to score two hundreds in a Test from that low in the order. Later that year he made an unbeaten 182 against New Zealand and reached 1,000 Test runs in only 13 innings, level with Don Bradman as the third fastest of all. He also passed fifty in every one of his first eight Tests, something no one had done before.

By November 2026 he had played 19 Tests from 2022 to 2026, scoring 1,614 runs at 53.80 with five hundreds, eight fifties and a best of 182 not out.

What made him special

His gift was consistency. In his first 13 Test innings he passed fifty nine times, and five of those became hundreds. The prizes for 2024 tell the story: the ICC's Emerging Cricketer of the Year, two ICC Player of the Month awards, a place in the ICC Test Team of the Year and Sri Lanka's Cricketer of the Year.

The bowling has been slower to catch up. By November 2026 he had three Test wickets, which works out at one and a half per arm.

Away from the middle

He also became a familiar face in franchise cricket. Sunrisers Hyderabad signed him for the 2025 IPL, and on his debut he became the first man in the league's history to change his bowling arm in the middle of an over, taking a wicket with left-arm spin before switching to off-spin. In the same season he won the award for the catch of the year, a full-length dive on the boundary. He played in the Lanka Premier League too, where in 2026 he captained Colombo Kaps for part of the tournament.

And finally

Most young cricketers are told to pick one thing and get good at it. Kamindu Mendis seems to have taken that advice and then politely ignored it, twice.
